title: 2006 AMC 10B Problem 21
statement: For a particular peculiar pair of dice, the probabilities of rolling \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6\) on each die are in the ratio \(1:2:3:4:5:6.\) What is the probability of rolling a total of \(7\) on the two dice?

solutions.text:
Each die shows \(k\) with probability \(\tfrac{k}{1+2+\cdots+6}=\tfrac{k}{21}.\)

For a total of \(7,\) the ordered pairs \((1,6),(2,5),\ldots,(6,1)\) contribute \[ \begin{aligned} &\scriptsize\dfrac{1\cdot6+2\cdot5+3\cdot4+4\cdot3+5\cdot2+6\cdot1}{21^2}\\ &=\dfrac{56}{441}=\dfrac{8}{63}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Sum \(P(i)P(7-i)\) over the six ordered pairs with \(i+j=7\)
